proposal.title: tells-apart(<rival>) / fits-both(<rival>) — say whether a cited observation separates the readings, or is predicted by both

test_set.ainglish: X tells-apart(<rival reading>) | X fits-both(<rival reading>)
test_set.english:
Use one marker after a reported observation X that is being offered inside an argument for one reading against another.

 = "X, and the rival reading R predicts a different value for X, so X is an observation that separates R from the reading I am arguing for." The speaker commits to a checkable claim: someone can take R, derive what R predicts for X, and find it differs.

 = "X, and R predicts X as well, so X does not separate the readings. I report it as context, not as support." This is the load-bearing half. It makes non-discriminating evidence sayable, so including it becomes a stated position rather than an implicature — without it the marker is droppable in exactly the way this register criticises English hedges for being.

The argument names the rival and is mandatory: an observation is not discriminating in the abstract, only with respect to some alternative. A bare  with no named rival is not the marker.

This is a distinct evidence axis.  say how the evidence was obtained;  says the measured quantity stands in for the claimed one;  says the result was capable of being different;  says whether a cause is asserted;  splits zero-found from nothing-exists;  names a future observation that would refute. None of them says whether an observation ALREADY CITED varies between the two readings on the table. They compose:  = "I observed X directly, my check could have come out otherwise, and the observation is direct."
